state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(piece_output_address) -> PROVED

watchme.trigger: every drive_brief that runs against a piece carrying `writes_to` — the drive record already carries `aider_reported_edited` and the before/after images, so the comparison costs nothing at the moment the drive lands.
watchme.enough: when 10 drives have been recorded and each one's reported edits fall inside the piece's declared `writes_to`, or at the FIRST drive whose edits all land outside it — that one is the finding and stops the watch immediately, because it means the declared address is not where the work actually goes and the field is decorative.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier carrying, per drive, the piece's `writes_to`, aider's `aider_reported_edited`, and the survival disposition of each path
watchme.nexus: the aider_shim drive record (drives.jsonl) — the same surface edit_survival_probe already reads
watchme.consumer: whoever next charts a ticket for the apprentice to build; today CC, deciding at decompose time whether a piece's output address is knowable, which is exactly the question this ticket's WRONG-INTENT clause names

intention: Give a decompose sub-problem a `writes_to` field — the addresses this piece's output lands at, whether or not they exist yet — and make it the source of aider's editable file list, demoting `uses` to read-only. Today nothing berthed says where a piece's work GOES. `uses` names survey holdings, and a holding is something the sweep FOUND, so a `build` piece's target is excluded from it by construction; `translate._files` nevertheless builds aider's editable `fnames` from `uses`, which means the apprentice is handed the files the piece READS and has to guess the file it must WRITE. The door (`write_decompose`) requires the field of new packets; the promotion judge (`judge_decompose`) checks only the field that is present, so the standing corpus is not retro-redded.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM, measured at the first live drive of aider-builds-a-piece piece 0: the brief handed the apprentice `venv.py` — a holding the piece names in `uses` — and the piece's actual job was to create a new general run-this-inside-the-venv verb. With no way to say where that verb goes, the model guessed `driver.py` and emitted an empty SEARCH block, which is aider's spelling of 'new file'. aider, holding driver.py open as editable, appended the new module body onto the end of it, putting `from __future__` at line 480. The edit was applied, the record said 'applied', and the repo had to be reverted by hand. That is the whole cost of the missing field at n=1, and it is a Law 1 failure at the last hop: the chain spent a stage settling how the work splits, and the module that turns a piece into a brief re-derives the target as a guess. CENSUS over the standing corpus: 51 decompose berths, 321 sub-problems, 320 carry `uses`, 0 carry any field naming an output address. The demotion of `uses` to read-only is a real tightening in its own right — today a holding a piece merely reads is handed to aider as editable, which is looser than constrain's own bounds.
traces_to: Law 1 — every answered question becomes structure; the chain answered 'where does this piece's work go' at decompose time and the answer had nowhere to berth, so the last hop re-derived it. Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by the schema, not by a hope that the model reads the prompt: the edit/read bound becomes aider's own fnames/read_only_fnames split, driven by a berthed field. Law 3 — the field makes a piece's target a checkable claim rather than an inference from prose.
gates: prove_gate: the tester runs the touched components' proofs under isolation (`python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --netns --seal --timeout 900 <dir>`) and seals a VALIDATION beside the code — verdict and seal from the same hand. Two addresses are touched and each proves at its own: cairn/devices/builder/machines/decompose/proofs/ for the door and the judge, cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/ for the brief. The judge's no-retro-red arm is proved against the REAL 51-berth corpus, not a fixture, because the claim is about the corpus. extra_gates: durability — committed and pushed, on the emit chokepoint; and the charter delta at each touched address pokes cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh in the same act. kicks_back_on: a red proof routes back to build at the point of creation (CP2). Bound additionally by this node's own shape: every new check is exercised by a mutation that removes it, and a mutant that breaks syntax is not a mutant.
falsifier: DONE when all four hold. (a) `write_decompose` REFUSES a packet in which any sub-problem lacks a non-empty `writes_to` list of non-empty in-repo addresses, with the lack named in the one-pass refusal alongside any other shape lack. (b) `judge_decompose` reds a piece whose `writes_to` names an address outside the cairn repo root or an existing DIRECTORY, and stays SILENT about a piece carrying no `writes_to` at all — proven by running the promotion-side judge over the real standing corpus of 51 berths and observing the decompose finding count UNCHANGED. (c) `translate.brief` builds aider's editable `fnames` from `writes_to` alone, puts `uses` into `read_only_fnames`, passes through a `writes_to` path that does not exist yet (a build piece's target is a file aider must CREATE — a skipped-because-unresolvable entry here would reproduce the exact defect), and refuses loudly with a re-chart message for a berth carrying no `writes_to`. (d) each new check is exercised by a mutation that removes it and a tooth that then fails. FALSIFIED IF the promotion sweep's decompose findings change against the standing corpus — a retro-red means the strictness is at the wrong mouth. WRONG-INTENT if a real piece's output genuinely cannot be named at decompose time: that would mean the split is being made before the target is knowable, and the fix would be upstream in the chain rather than a field here.
horizon: one build for the falsifier; the watch's horizon is 10 drives whose edits land inside the declared addresses, or the first drive whose edits all land outside, whichever comes first.
children: none. The seam is one schema field, its two mouths (the door hard, the promotion judge soft), and one downstream reader (translate._files) — splitting that into children would be ceremony. The one thing that could plausibly have been a child, the chain-staleness defect, is a different seam entirely (a freshness check between the berth and the drive) and is named in distinctions_recorded for its own cast rather than nested here.
dependencies: none. Both addresses exist and are proved; the standing 51-berth corpus is on disk and is the fixture the no-retro-red arm reads.
distinctions_recorded: THE TWO MOUTHS DIFFER IN STRICTNESS ON PURPOSE, AND THE CORPUS ALREADY RECORDS THAT AS A PATTERN. `_charted_packets` globs ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/decompose-*.json and keeps every packet claiming a ticket the component owns, so a hard `writes_to` requirement inside judge_decompose would red all 51 standing berths at the promotion gate — the same retro-red class as the trouble live in the inbox since 2026-08-16. The door requires the field of packets being written; the pure judge judges only what is present. survey_holdings_resolve's own docstring already names this asymmetry as deliberate rather than accidental.

`writes_to` DOES NOT HAVE TO BE A HOLDING, AND THAT IS NOT A HOLE IN THE SWEEP. decompose_composes_holdings exists because composition outside the measured inventory bypasses the sweep. A build piece creates what does not exist, so its target cannot be a holding — but the piece still has to name a MEASURED absence in `fills`, so the sweep still grounds it. What `writes_to` adds is where the answer to that absence goes, which the sweep by definition could not have found.

A `writes_to` PATH THAT DOES NOT RESOLVE MUST PASS THROUGH, NOT BE SKIPPED. `_files` today reports an unresolvable `uses` address as skipped, which is right for a holding — the piece claimed it exists. For an output address the opposite is true: a build piece's target is a file aider must CREATE, and skipping it would reproduce the exact defect this ticket fixes, at the exact function that fixes it.

NAMED AND DELIBERATELY OUT: THE CHAIN GOES STALE. Piece 0 of aider-builds-a-piece fills the measured absence 'a GENERAL run-this-inside-the-venv verb — venv.py has the pattern but keeps it private.' The decompose berth was taken at 14:05; run_in_venv went public in venv.py at 14:24 (cairn 634421d); the drive ran at 21:59 — seven and a half hours after the absence was filled. Nothing re-measures the survey between the berth and the drive, so a stale chain hands the apprentice finished work and the survival reading it produces is about nothing. That is a different seam and gets its own cast. This ticket's refusal for berths lacking the field forces a re-chart, and a re-chart incidentally re-measures — a side effect worth having, and not the fix.

intent_berth: none, because this entered at the TICKET door, not the INTENT door: it is a bug, and adding a field to the decompose sub-problem schema plus the two mouths that read it fixes it — no harmony of the system is broken and no intention was implemented contrary to its actual intention. /intent's charter names TICKET as one of the three entry points and directs bugs away from the birth questions explicitly.
